mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising the cost of capital and depressing corporate earnings growth, which in turn drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincides with weakening household demand, which reduces revenue expectations for consumer-facing firms and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly below zero at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 0.3 percentage points for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered periods at 90% confidence, or the mechanism fails during a period of simultaneous wage growth acceleration.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for four consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing activity, which reduces input demand and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 35% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and the Consumer Price Index above their respective 12-month averages signals a dual monetary tightening and inflationary pressure regime, which erodes real purchasing power and compresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism does not activate during a period of actual policy reversal.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent increase in both real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) and the housing starts index (HOUST) above their 6-month moving averages signals strengthening household balance sheets and housing demand, which boosts consumption and capital expenditure, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during triggered episodes at 95% confidence, or the mechanism fails when credit conditions tighten sharply.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate below 0.1 percentage points for six consecutive months despite steady or rising payroll employment (PAYEMS) indicates a shift in labor force participation rather than job losses, which historically coincides with stable consumer confidence and neutral S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE changes in [-0.1, 0.1] pp for 6 consecutive months AND PAYEMS >= 0% change
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism does not activate during a period of wage deflation.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in real personal savings (proxied by the residual of personal income minus consumption, RSAFS) above its 12-month average for five consecutive months signals elevated precautionary savings, which historically precedes a delayed but sustained consumer spending rebound and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during triggered episodes at 90% confidence, or the rebound in consumption does not materialize within the horizon.
